messages.text: Can you help me solve problem d in the last homework?
To differentiate \(2^{\sin x}\) use the chain rule: rewrite as \(e^{(\ln 2)\sin x}\). Differentiate \(e^u\) as \(e^u u'\). Need more help?
Can you help me solve second problem in the series homework? Should I use AST?
For a geometric series \(\sum a r^n\), check \(|r|<1\) to converge and use \(S=\frac{a}{1-r}\). Otherwise it diverges. Need help with a specific term?
Can I use the Alternating Series Test for the second problem in my series homework?

Only if the terms alternate sign. In \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n}{e^{n^2}}\) all terms are positive, so the Alternating Series Test doesn’t apply. Consider the Integral Test or a comparison test instead. Need more help?
Can I use the Alternating Series Test for the first problem in my series homework?

The Alternating Series Test only works for series whose terms alternate in sign. Since \(\frac{4n^2+3}{n^3}>0\) for all \(n\), the test isn’t applicable. Try a p‑series comparison instead. Need more help?
How can I use a p-series comparison
You can split \( \dfrac{4n^{2}+3}{n^{3}}=\dfrac{4}{n}+\dfrac{3}{n^{3}}\). Compare each part to a known p‑series: \(4/n\) diverges (\(p=1\)), \(3/n^{3}\) converges. Need more help?
So how can I know whether the total result converges or diverges?
Since \(4/n\) diverges, the whole sum diverges. Check by comparing to \(1/n\) or use a limit comparison test. Need help working that out?
Can you help me solve the first question in the series homework?
Try the comparison test: compare \(\frac{4n^{2}+3}{n^{3}}\) to \(\frac{4}{n}\).  Since \(\sum \frac{1}{n}\) diverges, so does this series. Need more help?
Great! Check the limit comparison: compute \(\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{(4n^2+3)/n^3}{4/n}\).  It should equal 1, confirming divergence. Need any step clarified?
